head: 146ccb3b1290ff50453a159e4cd70e4ed5b88b6b
summary: The scanner now charges every file at its own size, read from a metadata-only handle. It no longer uses the folder listing's figure. The only exceptions are cloud-only files and later names of a hardlinked file. The accepted M-add-1 shape is built: the scan thread lists everything, then ProbePass probes the files on BelowNormal worker threads a batch at a time. Each worker has its own cancel guard. The scan thread applies each batch only after that batch's workers finish, and ThreadOwner makes the single-writer rule structural. On local NTFS, outside OneDrive and cloud-marked folders, each folder is listed through a handle that keeps its last-access time (FILE_WRITE_ATTRIBUTES plus LastAccessTime -1). A folder that refuses this falls back to the plain open. Tests cover criteria 1, 3, 6 and 7 on a real temp tree, using tests/HoldRig, a separate process that holds files open and only observes through handles. The full default suite passes 370/370. The published exe charged a held file listed at 0 B at its own 300 MiB and left the folders' last-access times unchanged.

files.why: List-then-probe: the walk is unchanged, then SizeFiles builds batches of paths from the store, runs ProbePass, and applies readings on the scan thread. The inline repeat-FileId probe (_dueProbes/_settled/ProbeAndCorrect) is removed (M4). Correct and Credit call ThreadOwner.Check (M2). ProbeCorrected and VanishedBeforeProbe are recorded (m2, m5). The last-access decision is made once at the root (GetVolumeInformationByHandleW + FileRemoteProtocolInfo, M6), with OneDrive and cloud-attribute exclusion and asked/kept counters. There are phase timings (M5) and a sizing progress phase.

The probe workers (replaces the design's ProbePipeline, per M-add-1). Per batch it starts ProcessorCount-1 (1..15) BelowNormal background threads, each making its own SynchronousIoCancel. It never sees the store, and the scan thread applies results after all the batch's workers finish. A worker fault fails the scan. On cancel it waits 1 s, then leaves stuck workers, which hold only the batch's arrays (M3).
Structural single-writer check used by Scanner.Correct/Credit and ProbePass.Run (M2).

IsDue, IsWofSuspect and LargeFileThreshold are replaced by IsEligible (file, not cloud-only, not a later name). Adds IsGone for errors 2/3. Adds the ProbeFile and ProbeRule delegates used as test seams.

OpenDirectory(path, keepLastAccess, out handle) does the write-attributes open plus the LastAccessTime -1 set, falling back to a plain open, all in one bracketed call (M8 decision: the suppression lives here). KeptLastAccess. A static readonly FILE_BASIC_INFO payload checked at type load for size 40 and field offsets (m7). QueryFileSystemName. Class remark updated for per-worker guards.
Open/Read take keepLastAccess and pass it through to OpenDirectory.

FILE_WRITE_ATTRIBUTES, PINNED/UNPINNED, FileBasicInfo, FileRemoteProtocolInfo, ERROR_PATH_NOT_FOUND, the FILE_BASIC_INFO struct and its size, SetFileInformationByHandle, GetVolumeInformationByHandleW.
Test seams: Probe, ProbeRule (to run the replaced rule for B1's baseline), ProbeWorkers, ProbeBatch, ProbeAbandonAfter, SyncRoots.
Public VanishedBeforeProbe. Internal ProbeCorrections, ListingTime, SizingTime, LongestProbe, LastAccessAsked, LastAccessKept, for the tests and the validate re-measurement.
FilesToSize/FilesSized for the sizing phase (M-add-1 cost).
SizeProbed now means probed. New ProbeCorrected flag (m2).
Corrected(): publishes each applied batch's in-place corrections, at most once per interval.
The progress line shows 'Reading each file's own size: n of m' during sizing. New outcome note for files deleted before they could be sized (m5).
The held-open rig process, wired like CfProvider.

'hold' (CREATE_NEW, share none|read, backdates its own atime 48 h, grows in 1 MiB writes with no flush, READY, JSON self-report on 'report', holds until stdin EOF) and 'snapshot' (FILE_READ_ATTRIBUTES-only handle reads of the four times, EOF, allocation and attributes; never lists).
Launches HoldRig through the runtime's dotnet.exe and the test runtimeconfig. A held file is killed if it is still alive 10 s after stdin closes.

One fixture, one real temp tree: criteria 1, 3, 6 and 7, the positive control, and the old-rule baseline, with the observation discipline B1 requires. Records the fsutil state and the pre-scan listing readings in the test output.
C-008 kept-vs-plain listing, the M7 write-attributes-refusal fallback, sync-root exclusion, the local-NTFS gate, IsAtOrUnder, and the FILE_BASIC_INFO layout.
C-012, C-013 (reworked per M4), M3 worker fault / stuck-worker cancel / interruptible cancel, per-worker guard and priority (m4, M5), ThreadOwner (M2), vanished file and no-FileId (m5).

m1: renamed to AFileWhoseListingSaysNothingIsAllocatedIsProbedUnlessItIsCloudOnly, with every old-gate assertion rewritten (Probes 4, all-hole and resident SizeProbed, the cloud guards kept). New C-011 test ASmallFileWhoseListingSaysNothingIsChargedAtItsOwnSize. Probe counts and flags updated.
C-011: ALoneNameUnderTheRootIsChargedAtItsListingSize rewritten as ...AtItsOwnSize. Flags and comments updated for first-name probing, with no repeat probe (M4).
Probes now run after the walk, so the scan-thread cancel sweep expects no probes and no SizeProbed. The repeat-probe special case is removed (M4). Call sites pass keepLastAccess.
The two-scan comparison masks ProbeCorrected: the first scan's probe refreshes the stale name's directory entry (SL-045). Pinned as ProbeCorrections 1 then 0.
Every file probed through its \\?\ path (6 probes, ProbeFailures 0). a. is probed through its own name.
Comments and flags updated: the stale name's own probe corrects it after the walk.
OpenDirectory call sites pass keepLastAccess: true.
Listing reads the way the scan reads, keeping the folder's last-access time.
InteropLivesOnlyInNative exempts tests\HoldRig\ (twinned with fitness.yaml).
ProjectReference to tests/HoldRig.
Lists tests/HoldRig.

Twinned InteropLivesOnlyInNative (both copies) excepts tests/HoldRig/**. SL-056 settled block rewritten: rule 1 targets ProbePass.cs and all store writes (M2). Rule 2 fences every timestamp/attribute setter, except Kernel32.cs and SynchronousIoCancel.cs (M8). Rule 3 widened to Scanning/*.cs with corrected because-text (m3). New rule 4: only DirectoryReader lists (M8).

Design as built: rule, shape, cancel/fault, counters and consumer inventory, last-access gates and limits, observation discipline, drive-time and network notes, rules, corrected citations (m8), case-to-test map.
Marks the three-case SizeProbe, the accepted under-64-MiB gap (:97), repeat-name probe paths, and probe-before-append as superseded by SL-056.

obligations.how: C-001: HeldOpenTreeTests.AFileAnotherProcessIsGrowingIsChargedAtItsOwnSize. HoldRig grows grow.bin to 257 MiB, share Read, in another process. The listing reads (0,0) as the last step before the scan (recorded). The scan charges the holder-reported EOF/allocation with SizeProbed|ProbeCorrected. It fails under the old gate (manual mutation and the seam baseline).

C-003: HeldOpenTreeTests.AFileHeldWithNoSharingIsChargedAtItsOwnSize. locked.bin is held by another process with FileShare.None and listed at (0,0). It is charged at its holder-reported size, with ProbeFailures 0.

C-006: HeldOpenTreeTests.TheScanChangesNoEntrysMetadata. All four times, EOF, allocation and attributes of every non-held entry are read before and after by HoldRig's handle-only snapshot; held files are read through their holders' own handles. It asserts each entry was back-dated, and that every folder's listing kept last-access (8 of 8, in both scans). fsutil disablelastaccess is recorded in the output: 'DisableLastAccess = 2 (System Managed, Last Access Time Updates ENABLED)'.

C-007: HeldOpenTreeTests.APlainListingOfTheControlFolderMovesItsLastAccessTime. A back-dated control folder outside the root is listed plainly by the test process. The same HoldRig observer must see its last-access time move by more than 1 h.

C-008: LastAccessTests.AListingThatKeepsTheLastAccessTimeLeavesItWhereAPlainOneMovesIt. The same DirectoryReader.Read on two back-dated folders: with keepLastAccess the atime is unchanged and KeptLastAccess is true; without it the atime moves (built-in control).

C-010: HeldOpenTreeTests.EachFolderIsTheOnDiskBytesBelowIt. Every folder's rolled size, on-disk size and file count are checked against totals computed without the scan: plain files from the snapshot, held files from holders' reports, and the hardlinked file once, charged to links\a-first (the first-met name, m6).

C-011: OnDiskSizeTests.ASmallFileWhoseListingSaysNothingIsChargedAtItsOwnSize (3 MiB, listed at 0 B, not WOF-suspect) and HardlinkTests.ALoneNameUnderTheRootIsChargedAtItsOwnSize (the old Probes==0 test rewritten to Probes 1 at 64 MiB). Both failed under the old gate in the mutation run.

C-012: ProbePassTests.TheScanEndsOnlyOnceEveryProbeIsApplied. Uses 4-file batches and a probe seam that adds +7 bytes. It asserts no probe starts before every folder is listed, and that on return every file carries the probe's figure; FilesSized == FilesToSize == 15.

C-013 as it now stands, after M4 removed the inline correction: ProbePassTests.ALaterNameMetBeforeTheFirstNamesProbeIsNeverProbedOrCharged. The later name is listed before the first name's probe starts, which is observed. Only the first name's path is probed; it is charged once at 64 MiB to its folder, and the later name is charged 0.

B1: (1) nothing opens a held file or the stale name before the scan returns; held files are observed via their holders, the hardlink via its written-through name. (2) Snapshot first; the listing check is the last step before the scan (using the kept listing) and is recorded. (3) Criterion 7 totals come from holder reports and handle snapshots, and post-scan snapshots are taken only afterwards. (4) The ProbeCorrected flag shows the scan, not the listing, supplied the figure. (5) Baseline: an old-rule scan runs first via ScanOptions.ProbeRule, and TheRuleSl056ReplacedFailsCriteria1_3And7 asserts the criteria 1, 3 and 7 checks fail under it. A manual mutation (old gate in Scanner's default rule) failed those Facts plus both C-011 tests; the file was restored and its hash matched. (6) The 'until the scanner lists it' reading is recorded in the design doc and the test remarks.

M2: ThreadOwner records the owning thread. Scanner.Run's Correct and Credit, and ProbePass.Run, throw off it. Workers receive paths and return readings, with no apply delegate, and ProbePass cannot name ScanStore. The regex rule is kept and widened (CorrectSizes, AddFlags). Test: ProbePassTests.TheStoresWriterAndTheProbePassRefuseEveryOtherThread.

M3, adapted to the list-then-probe shape, which has no Submit to block. A cancelled batch ends through ScanStatus.Cancelled and commits nothing, and the wait is bounded (1 s, then stuck workers are left; they hold no store). A worker fault stops the others and Scan throws InvalidOperationException (inner = the fault). Injectable probe seam (ScanOptions.Probe). Tests: AProbeWorkerThatThrowsFailsTheScanInsteadOfHanging, CancelWhileWorkersAreStuckEndsTheScanCancelledWithinTheBound, CancelInterruptsTheCallAWorkerIsBlockedIn.

M4: the inline ProbeAndCorrect branch, _settled and _dueProbes are removed, and repeats are dedup-only. The race case is replaced by C-013's reworked test. Expectations updated in HardlinkTests, LongPathTests, TopLevelTests, CancelledFolderTests and CancellationTests.

M5: (1) ScanResult exposes ListingTime, SizingTime, LongestProbe, LastAccessAsked and LastAccessKept (fallback opens) for validate to report per phase; drains no longer exist. (2) The inline probe is dropped. (3) The measured sequential shape is the primary one, and a time miss is advisory (design record). (4) Workers run at BelowNormal (asserted in ProbesRunOnBackgroundWorkersBelowNormalEachWithItsOwnGuard).

M6: suppression is asked only when the root's volume reports NTFS and refuses FileRemoteProtocolInfo, i.e. is local; SMB, ReFS, FAT and exFAT get the plain open. Sync roots are excluded rather than checked: folders at or under the OneDrive roots the environment names, and folders carrying RECALL/OFFLINE/PINNED/UNPINNED, are listed plainly (NothingUnderASyncRootIsAskedToKeepItsLastAccessTime). The narrower guarantee is recorded next to the ACL limit. Residual: another sync engine's root without those attributes is not recognised.

M7, made material: LastAccessTests.AFolderThatRefusesWriteAttributesIsListedPlainlyAndCountedInFull. A deny ACE for FILE_WRITE_ATTRIBUTES only; the folder is listed, its children counted, it is not unreadable, asked/kept = 4/3, and the other three folders keep their times. The contract is reworded in code and docs: only a failed plain open records a folder unreadable.

M8: the suppression lives inside SynchronousIoCancel.OpenDirectory. Rule 2 now fences SetFileInformationByHandle, SetFileTime, NtSetInformationFile, SetFileAttributes*, File/Directory.Set*Time and .*Time(Utc) =, excepting Kernel32.cs and SynchronousIoCancel.cs. New rule: only DirectoryReader lists a directory (FindFirstFile, NtQueryDirectoryFile, the directory-info classes, Directory.Enumerate/Get*, FileSystemEnumerable). A simulated code-only match found 0 hits in the tree and hits on planted violations.

m1: I read the whole test. It is renamed AFileWhoseListingSaysNothingIsAllocatedIsProbedUnlessItIsCloudOnly, and every old-gate assertion is rewritten: Probes 4, all-hole and resident are SizeProbed, ProbeCorrections 1, and the cloud-only assertions for both OFFLINE files are kept.

m2: new EntryFlags.ProbeCorrected and ScanResult.ProbeCorrections. A consumer search of the App, WindowReport, tests/window and eng found no reader of SizeProbed or Probes outside Core and its tests. The App reads only ProbeFailures (plus the new VanishedBeforeProbe and progress fields). The inventory is recorded in the design doc.
m3: rule 3's files widened to src/FsAnalyser.Core/Scanning/*.cs. The because-text now says a route change turns the criterion-5 test red, and that the risk is someone 'fixing' the fixture.

m5: errors 2/3 are counted in VanishedBeforeProbe, kept apart from ProbeFailures, and the listing figure is kept (AFileDeletedBeforeItsProbeKeepsItsListingSizesAndIsNoFailure). An entry with no usable FileId is first-seen and probed (AnEntryWithNoFileIdIsProbedAsAFirstName). The replaced-file case is accepted in the design record.

m6: the hardlink's names sit in links\a-first (stale, met first by name order) and links\b-second (written through). Criterion 7's expectation charges the file once to a-first; b-second holds 1 file and 0 bytes.

m7: a single static readonly FILE_BASIC_INFO payload. At type load, SynchronousIoCancel checks sizeof/Marshal.SizeOf == 40 with LastAccessTime at offset 8 and FileAttributes at 32, and throws PlatformNotSupportedException otherwise (also tested in TheBasicInfoPayloadHasTheLayoutWindowsReads). Recording EnableControlledFolderAccess is assigned to validate in the design record; I did not read Defender settings.

m8: the design record's prior art drops 'or a threshold is crossed', adds SL-045's refresh-on-open, cites U-012 for the cost claim, and replaces the exchangetuts URL with https://stackoverflow.com/questions/7828132/.

M-add-1: list-then-probe-then-apply is the baseline, and the overlapped bounded pipeline is not built. Deviation: results are applied per 32,768-file batch after that batch's workers finish, not after one whole-drive join, so memory stays bounded (see deviations). The design record states the ~90 s tail and the sizing progress phase, and removes the advisory-versus-resynthesis contradiction.

M-add-2: the design record states that every probe on a network volume is its own create/query/close round trip and that nothing limits this by volume type. It assigns validate the loopback-SMB re-measurement (per-probe latency and total probe time beside listing time), with a person deciding if the ratio is large. I did not measure it: the rig changes this machine's SMB client mappings.

deviations: Batches instead of one whole-drive join (M-add-1). The fix described one results array applied after one join. At ~4M files that is ~100 MiB of paths and readings, most of the headroom SL-042/SL-044 measured under 1 GiB, and M-add-1's own decision marks it unmeasured. I built the same list-then-probe-then-apply shape per 32,768-file batch: the scan thread applies a batch only after all its workers have finished, so single-writer and apply ordering hold per batch exactly as for one join.
The design's ProbePipeline.cs (Submit/Drain/Complete, capacity 8192) became ProbePass.cs (Run per batch), because M-add-1 replaced the overlapped pipeline. Settled rule 1 now targets ProbePass.cs.

M3's fix names Submit and a linked token. This shape has no Submit, so nothing can block there. I kept the rest: a bounded wait on cancel that leaves stuck workers (which hold no store), cancel ending as ScanStatus.Cancelled, a worker fault failing the scan, and the injectable probe seam with fault and cancel tests.

M6's sync-root exclusion recognises sync roots only through the OneDrive environment variables and cloud folder attributes, not a general sync-root lookup. cldapi is banned in src by the SL-049 rule, the registry is off-limits here, and in a standalone exe placeholders hide their tags (U-004). The CfProvider check was not run because it registers a real sync root, a question SL-049 left open for a person.

Case C-013 as designed (an async result after an inline correction) cannot occur once M4 removed the inline repeat probe. Its test feeds the same shape (a later name met before the first name's probe) and asserts the invariant it protected: one charge, at the true size, to the first name's folder.
Beyond the design, the App gained a sizing progress line and a vanished-files note. These are the consumers M-add-1 ('progress reporting needs a sizing phase') and m5 ('report separately') call for.
not_built: The overlapped bounded ProbePipeline (Submit/Drain/Complete, capacity 8192, concurrent with the listing): replaced by list-then-probe per accepted M-add-1.
The inline repeat-FileId probe that the design kept as a fallback lever: removed per accepted M4.

The M6 option of running the atime spike through the opt-in CfProvider sync root: not built or run, because it registers a real cldflt sync root on this PC, which SL-049 left for a person. OneDrive roots and cloud-marked folders are excluded instead.

The drive-time re-measurement on C: and the loopback-SMB probe-cost measurement: these are validate's work per the design and M-add-2. The counters they need (ListingTime, SizingTime, LongestProbe, LastAccessAsked/Kept) are built.
Recording Get-MpPreference EnableControlledFolderAccess: assigned to validate by the m7 decision. I did not read Defender settings.
Surfacing folders that refuse write-attributes in the scan result (the design's open question): not built. Only the internal LastAccessAsked/LastAccessKept counters exist, pending a person's answer.
follow_ups: Recognise sync roots from any cloud-files engine (Dropbox, Google Drive, iCloud), not only OneDrive via the environment, or get a person's go-ahead to run the opt-in CfProvider check (placeholder in-sync state unchanged, no provider callbacks) before keeping last-access inside sync roots.

Validate: run a whole-drive C:\ scan with the built scanner and report ListingTime, SizingTime, LongestProbe and LastAccessAsked vs LastAccessKept against the spike's 188.3 s sequential baseline. I did not run it unattended because it issues the keep-last-access SetFileInformationByHandle call (measured as a no-op) on the person's own profile folders.
Validate: with a person's go-ahead, repeat the re-measurement through the SMB loopback rig and report per-probe latency beside listing time (M-add-2).
Add a settled rule fencing tests/HoldRig from FsAnalyser.Core (no ProjectReference, no FsAnalyser.Core name), as CfProvider has, so the observer stays independent of the code it checks.

The window's last progress tick can show pre-correction totals: C:\Program Files ended with CountersText at 32.0 GB on disk against the outcome's 32.1 GB, because the final batch lands after the last 250 ms tick. The pattern predates this slice, but sizing at the end makes it likelier; showing the final totals in CountersText at the ending would remove it.

A person answers the design's open question: should folders that refuse write-attributes (the majority on C:\Windows and Program Files) be surfaced in the scan result, rather than only counted internally?

tests.command: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 build tests/HoldRig/HoldRig.csproj -c Debug -o %TEMP%\sl056-holdrig, then two HoldRig 'hold' processes (257 MiB share read, 32 MiB share none) listed with Get-ChildItem at +0/+5/+15 s
tests.note: Premise check before building on it: both files listed 0 B while held (15 s and after self-reports), and caught up only when the handles closed (269,484,032 and 33,554,432).

tests.command: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 build FsAnalyser.slnx -c Debug
tests.note: 0 warnings, 0 errors (final state). One intermediate build failed with CS0136 in LastAccessTests, which I fixed.

First run: 31/32. The fallback test's back-dated refusing\sub read back 'now' because TempTree.Deny (SetNamedSecurityInfo) propagates inheritance and lists the subtree. A throwaway experiment showed the scan leaves sub alone. The test now back-dates after the deny and proves the fallback through counters plus three kept folders.

Intermediate full run: 368/370. One failure came from stale binaries of the fallback test (the build had failed). The other was a real consequence in CancellationTests (stale hardlink): the first scan's probe refreshes the stale entry (SL-045), so the second scan has no ProbeCorrected. Fixed by masking that flag and pinning ProbeCorrections 1 then 0.
Final full default suite: 370 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, 21 s (was 337 before). Includes ArchitectureRulesTests and RuleCopiesAgreeTests.

tests.command: Mutation: Scanner.cs default ProbeRule replaced with the old gate (WOF suspect or listed >= 64 MiB), then eng/dotnet.ps1 test --filter HeldOpenTreeTests|OnDiskSizeTests.ASmallFileWhoseListingSaysNothingIsChargedAtItsOwnSize|HardlinkTests.ALoneNameUnderTheRootIsChargedAtItsOwnSize
tests.note: Failed on purpose (B1 baseline): criteria 1, 3 and 7 Facts and both C-011 tests failed (5 of 8; the criterion-6, control and seam-baseline Facts are rule-independent). File restored with hash 5C74A947...5949 identical; after a touch and rebuild, 8/8 pass.

Recorded: fsutil 'DisableLastAccess = 2 (System Managed, Last Access Time Updates ENABLED)'. Listed before scan: grow.bin (0,0), locked.bin (0,0), stale.bin 1,048,576. Own handles: grow.bin 269,484,032/273,285,120, locked.bin 25,165,824/32,505,856. 6 probes, 3 corrected, last access kept 8 of 8.

pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/read-window.ps1 -Root <temp folder with HoldRig holding grow.bin at 300 MiB, listed 0 B>
tests.note: Shipped exe via its real entry point: EXIT 0, 'Finished', '2 files ... 300.0 MB in files, taking 303.5 MB on disk', matching the holder's own EOF 314,572,800 / allocation 318,242,816 plus plain.txt. A second run on the same folder with back-dated root and sub left both last-access times unchanged, while a plain listing afterwards moved sub's (control).

Real input: EXIT 0, Finished, 77,523 files, 10,447 folders, 30 links not followed, 32.0 GB in files / 32.1 GB on disk, read in 2.1 s (warm). No probe-failure or vanished notes; 3 unreadable folders were already unreadable before this change. The last CountersText tick showed 32.0 GB on disk against the outcome's 32.1 (see follow-ups). A whole-drive C:\ run was deliberately not done (see follow-ups).
